From 2091c6aa0df6aba47deb5c8ab232b1cb60af3519 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Weiming Shi <bestswngs@gmail.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2026 19:46:54 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] openvswitch: cap upcall PID array size and pre-size vport
 replies

The vport netlink reply helpers allocate a fixed-size skb with
nlmsg_new(NLMSG_DEFAULT_SIZE, ...) but serialize the full upcall PID
array via ovs_vport_get_upcall_portids().  Since
ovs_vport_set_upcall_portids() accepts any non-zero multiple of
sizeof(u32) with no upper bound, a CAP_NET_ADMIN user can install a PID
array large enough to overflow the reply buffer, causing nla_put() to
fail with -EMSGSIZE and hitting BUG_ON(err < 0).  On systems with
unprivileged user namespaces enabled (e.g., Ubuntu default), this is
reachable via unshare -Urn since OVS vport mutation operations use
GENL_UNS_ADMIN_PERM.

 kernel BUG at net/openvswitch/datapath.c:2414!
 Oops: invalid opcode: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN NOPTI
 CPU: 1 UID: 0 PID: 65 Comm: poc Not tainted 7.0.0-rc7-00195-geb216e422044 #1
 RIP: 0010:ovs_vport_cmd_set+0x34c/0x400
 Call Trace:
  <TASK>
  genl_family_rcv_msg_doit (net/netlink/genetlink.c:1116)
  genl_rcv_msg (net/netlink/genetlink.c:1194)
  netlink_rcv_skb (net/netlink/af_netlink.c:2550)
  genl_rcv (net/netlink/genetlink.c:1219)
  netlink_unicast (net/netlink/af_netlink.c:1344)
  netlink_sendmsg (net/netlink/af_netlink.c:1894)
  __sys_sendto (net/socket.c:2206)
  __x64_sys_sendto (net/socket.c:2209)
  do_syscall_64 (arch/x86/entry/syscall_64.c:63)
  entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe (arch/x86/entry/entry_64.S:130)
  </TASK>
 Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception

Reject attempts to set more PIDs than nr_cpu_ids in
ovs_vport_set_upcall_portids(), and pre-compute the worst-case reply
size in ovs_vport_cmd_msg_size() based on that bound, similar to the
existing ovs_dp_cmd_msg_size().  nr_cpu_ids matches the cap already
used by the per-CPU dispatch configuration on the datapath side
(ovs_dp_cmd_fill_info() serialises at most nr_cpu_ids PIDs), so the
two sides stay consistent.

Fixes: 5cd667b0a456 ("openvswitch: Allow each vport to have an array of 'port_id's.")
Reported-by: Xiang Mei <xmei5@asu.edu>
Assisted-by: Claude:claude-opus-4-6
Signed-off-by: Weiming Shi <bestswngs@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Ilya Maximets <i.maximets@ovn.org>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260416024653.153456-2-bestswngs@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/net/openvswitch/vport.c b/net/openvswitch/vport.c
index 23f629e94a36..56b2e2d1a749 100644
--- a/net/openvswitch/vport.c
+++ b/net/openvswitch/vport.c
@@ -406,6 +406,9 @@ int ovs_vport_set_upcall_portids(struct vport *vport, const struct nlattr *ids)
 	if (!nla_len(ids) || nla_len(ids) % sizeof(u32))
 		return -EINVAL;
 
+	if (nla_len(ids) / sizeof(u32) > nr_cpu_ids)
+		return -EINVAL;
+
 	old = ovsl_dereference(vport->upcall_portids);
 
 	vport_portids = kmalloc(sizeof(*vport_portids) + nla_len(ids),
-- 
2.34.1



diff --git a/net/openvswitch/datapath.c b/net/openvswitch/datapath.c
index e209099218b4..bbbde50fc649 100644
--- a/net/openvswitch/datapath.c
+++ b/net/openvswitch/datapath.c
@@ -2184,9 +2184,40 @@ static int ovs_vport_cmd_fill_info(struct vport *vport, struct sk_buff *skb,
 	return err;
 }
 
+static size_t ovs_vport_cmd_msg_size(void)
+{
+	size_t msgsize = NLMSG_ALIGN(sizeof(struct ovs_header));
+
+	msgsize += nla_total_size(sizeof(u32)); /* OVS_VPORT_ATTR_PORT_NO */
+	msgsize += nla_total_size(sizeof(u32)); /* OVS_VPORT_ATTR_TYPE */
+	msgsize += nla_total_size(IFNAMSIZ);    /* OVS_VPORT_ATTR_NAME */
+	msgsize += nla_total_size(sizeof(u32)); /* OVS_VPORT_ATTR_IFINDEX */
+	msgsize += nla_total_size(sizeof(s32)); /* OVS_VPORT_ATTR_NETNSID */
+
+	/* OVS_VPORT_ATTR_STATS */
+	msgsize += nla_total_size_64bit(sizeof(struct ovs_vport_stats));
+
+	/* OVS_VPORT_ATTR_UPCALL_STATS(OVS_VPORT_UPCALL_ATTR_SUCCESS +
+	 *                             OVS_VPORT_UPCALL_ATTR_FAIL)
+	 */
+	msgsize += nla_total_size(nla_total_size_64bit(sizeof(u64)) +
+				  nla_total_size_64bit(sizeof(u64)));
+
+	/* OVS_VPORT_ATTR_UPCALL_PID */
+	msgsize += nla_total_size(nr_cpu_ids * sizeof(u32));
+
+	/* OVS_VPORT_ATTR_OPTIONS(OVS_TUNNEL_ATTR_DST_PORT +
+	 *                        OVS_TUNNEL_ATTR_EXTENSION(OVS_VXLAN_EXT_GBP))
+	 */
+	msgsize += nla_total_size(nla_total_size(sizeof(u16)) +
+				  nla_total_size(nla_total_size(0)));
+
+	return msgsize;
+}
+
 static struct sk_buff *ovs_vport_cmd_alloc_info(void)
 {
-	return nlmsg_new(NLMSG_DEFAULT_SIZE, GFP_KERNEL);
+	return genlmsg_new(ovs_vport_cmd_msg_size(), GFP_KERNEL);
 }
 
 /* Called with ovs_mutex, only via ovs_dp_notify_wq(). */
@@ -2196,7 +2227,7 @@ struct sk_buff *ovs_vport_cmd_build_info(struct vport *vport, struct net *net,
 	struct sk_buff *skb;
 	int retval;
 
-	skb = nlmsg_new(NLMSG_DEFAULT_SIZE, GFP_KERNEL);
+	skb = ovs_vport_cmd_alloc_info();
 	if (!skb)
 		return ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM);

## Summary of Patch Modifications

### Modifications in Each File:

1. **`net/openvswitch/vport.c`** (line 409)
   - **Added validation:** Reject attempts to set upcall PID arrays larger than `nr_cpu_ids`. The check ensures `nla_len(ids) / sizeof(u32) > nr_cpu_ids` returns `-EINVAL`, capping the number of PIDs to the number of CPUs.

2. **`net/openvswitch/datapath.c`** (lines 2187–2230)
   - **Added `ovs_vport_cmd_msg_size()` function:** Computes the worst-case Netlink message size needed for a vport reply, including the full upcall PID array (sized as `nr_cpu_ids * sizeof(u32)`) and all other fixed-size attributes.
   - **Updated `ovs_vport_cmd_alloc_info()`:** Changed from `nlmsg_new(NLMSG_DEFAULT_SIZE, ...)` to `genlmsg_new(ovs_vport_cmd_msg_size(), ...)`, ensuring the allocated skb is always large enough.
   - **Updated `ovs_vport_cmd_build_info()`:** Replaced direct `nlmsg_new(NLMSG_DEFAULT_SIZE, ...)` with a call to `ovs_vport_cmd_alloc_info()` for consistency.

### Relationship Between the Modifications:

- **Root cause:** A CAP_NET_ADMIN user could install an arbitrarily large upcall PID array, causing the vport reply to overflow the fixed-size `NLMSG_DEFAULT_SIZE` skb, leading to a kernel BUG.
- **Solution pairing:**  
  - The **cap in `vport.c`** limits the PID array to `nr_cpu_ids`, preventing oversized arrays from being stored.  
  - The **pre-sized reply buffer in `datapath.c`** uses the same `nr_cpu_ids` limit to compute the worst-case message size, ensuring the allocated skb can always accommodate the maximum possible PID array.  
- **Consistency:** Both changes use `nr_cpu_ids` as the upper bound, matching the per-CPU dispatch logic already in place on the datapath side (`ovs_dp_cmd_fill_info` serializes at most `nr_cpu_ids` PIDs). This ensures the two sides remain in sync.

2.34.1

The patch addresses a vulnerability in the Open vSwitch (OVS) module where a `CAP_NET_ADMIN` user could install an overly large `upcall_portids` array, causing a `BUG_ON` due to a stack buffer overflow in netlink reply handling.

**Modifications in each file:**

- **`net/openvswitch/vport.c`**:
  - In `ovs_vport_set_upcall_portids()`, added a sanity check to reject any `upcall_portids` array whose length exceeds `nr_cpu_ids` (when expressed as number of `u32` elements). This caps the maximum PID count to the number of CPUs, matching the existing upper bound used elsewhere in the datapath.

- **`net/openvswitch/datapath.c`**:
  - Added a new helper function `ovs_vport_cmd_msg_size()` that calculates the exact worst-case size of a vport netlink reply, including `nla_total_size(nr_cpu_ids * sizeof(u32))` for the `OVS_VPORT_ATTR_UPCALL_PID` attribute. This ensures the reply buffer is always large enough.
  - Changed `ovs_vport_cmd_alloc_info()` to use `genlmsg_new(ovs_vport_cmd_msg_size(), GFP_KERNEL)` instead of `nlmsg_new(NLMSG_DEFAULT_SIZE, ...)`, so the allocated skb is sized correctly upfront.
  - Changed `ovs_vport_cmd_build_info()` to call `ovs_vport_cmd_alloc_info()` instead of directly calling `nlmsg_new(NLMSG_DEFAULT_SIZE, ...)`, ensuring consistent sizing when building reply skbs.

**Relationship between the modifications:**

The two changes are complementary. The cap in `vport.c` prevents the PID array from exceeding the maximum number of CPUs (`nr_cpu_ids`). The pre‑computed size in `datapach.c` uses the same bound to guarantee that the reply skb is allocated with enough space to hold the largest possible PID array. Together, they eliminate the buffer overflow condition that triggered the `BUG_ON` during serialization of a vport’s upcall PID list.

The patch addresses a buffer overflow vulnerability in Open vSwitch (OVS) where a user with `CAP_NET_ADMIN` could install an excessively large upcall PID array, causing the vport netlink reply to overflow a fixed-size buffer and trigger a kernel BUG. The fix consists of two coordinated changes:

### Modifications

1. **File: `net/openvswitch/vport.c`**  
   - In `ovs_vport_set_upcall_portids()`, added a check that the number of PIDs provided in the netlink attribute does not exceed `nr_cpu_ids`. This caps the maximum allowed PID array size, preventing installation of oversized arrays that would later cause buffer overflow when the vport info is serialized.

2. **File: `net/openvswitch/datapath.c`**  
   - Added a new static function `ovs_vport_cmd_msg_size()` that computes the worst-case size needed for a vport netlink reply message. It sums the `nla_total_size` of all fixed fields and uses `nla_total_size(nr_cpu_ids * sizeof(u32))` for the upcall PID array, matching the new cap.  
   - Updated `ovs_vport_cmd_alloc_info()` to call `genlmsg_new(ovs_vport_cmd_msg_size(), GFP_KERNEL)` instead of `nlmsg_new(NLMSG_DEFAULT_SIZE, ...)`, ensuring the allocated skb is large enough for any valid vport (including one with the maximum allowed PID array).  
   - Updated `ovs_vport_cmd_build_info()` to use `ovs_vport_cmd_alloc_info()` instead of directly calling `nlmsg_new(NLMSG_DEFAULT_SIZE, ...)`, so that the info-reply skb is also pre-sized correctly.

### Relationships

- The **cap on PID array size** (in `vport.c`) prevents the root cause: users can no longer store an array larger than `nr_cpu_ids`.  
- The **pre-sized reply buffer** (in `datapath.c`) guarantees that even the most demanding valid vport (with `nr_cpu_ids` PIDs) will fit into the allocated skb, avoiding the `-EMSGSIZE` error and subsequent `BUG_ON`.  
- Together, these changes enforce consistency: the vport-side storage limit (`nr_cpu_ids` PIDs) matches the worst-case serialization assumption in the netlink reply path. This eliminates the overflow vulnerability while maintaining correct behavior for all allowed configurations.

Here is the root cause:
The vport upcall PID array size is not capped in `ovs_vport_set_upcall_portids()`, allowing a user to set an arbitrarily large array. When the vport info is serialized in `ovs_vport_cmd_fill_info()`, the fixed-size skb allocated with `NLMSG_DEFAULT_SIZE` overflows, causing `nla_put()` to fail with `-EMSGSIZE` and triggering `BUG_ON(err < 0)` in `datapath.c`.

Here is the patch:
 
+static size_t ovs_vport_cmd_msg_size(void)
+{
+	size_t msgsize = NLMSG_ALIGN(sizeof(struct ovs_header));
+
+	msgsize += nla_total_size(sizeof(u32)); /* OVS_VPORT_ATTR_PORT_NO */
+	msgsize += nla_total_size(sizeof(u32)); /* OVS_VPORT_ATTR_TYPE */
+	msgsize += nla_total_size(IFNAMSIZ);    /* OVS_VPORT_ATTR_NAME */
+	msgsize += nla_total_size(sizeof(u32)); /* OVS_VPORT_ATTR_IFINDEX */
+	msgsize += nla_total_size(sizeof(s32)); /* OVS_VPORT_ATTR_NETNSID */
+
+	/* OVS_VPORT_ATTR_STATS */
+	msgsize += nla_total_size_64bit(sizeof(struct ovs_vport_stats));
+
+	/* OVS_VPORT_ATTR_UPCALL_STATS(OVS_VPORT_UPCALL_ATTR_SUCCESS +
+	 *                             OVS_VPORT_UPCALL_ATTR_FAIL)
+	 */
+	msgsize += nla_total_size(nla_total_size_64bit(sizeof(u64)) +
+				  nla_total_size_64bit(sizeof(u64)));
+
+	/* OVS_VPORT_ATTR_UPCALL_PID */
+	msgsize += nla_total_size(nr_cpu_ids * sizeof(u32));
+
+	/* OVS_VPORT_ATTR_OPTIONS(OVS_TUNNEL_ATTR_DST_PORT +
+	 *                        OVS_TUNNEL_ATTR_EXTENSION(OVS_VXLAN_EXT_GBP))
+	 */
+	msgsize += nla_total_size(nla_total_size(sizeof(u16)) +
+				  nla_total_size(nla_total_size(0)));
+
+	return msgsize;
+}
+
 static struct sk_buff *ovs_vport_cmd_alloc_info(void)
 {
-	return nlmsg_new(NLMSG_DEFAULT_SIZE, GFP_KERNEL);
+	return genlmsg_new(ovs_vport_cmd_msg_size(), GFP_KERNEL);
 }
 
 /* Called with ovs_mutex, only via ovs_dp_notify_wq(). */
 struct sk_buff *ovs_vport_cmd_build_info(struct vport *vport, struct net *net,
 					 u32 portid, u32 seq, u8 cmd)
 {
 	struct sk_buff *skb;
 	int retval;
 
-	skb = nlmsg_new(NLMSG_DEFAULT_SIZE, GFP_KERNEL);
+	skb = ovs_vport_cmd_alloc_info();
 	if (!skb)
 		return ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM);
 
 	retval = ovs_vport_cmd_fill_info(vport, skb, net, portid, seq, 0, cmd,
 					 GFP_KERNEL);
 	BUG_ON(retval < 0);
 
 	return skb;
 }

Root cause:
The vport upcall PID array size is not capped in `ovs_vport_set_upcall_portids()`, allowing a user to set an arbitrarily large array. When the vport info is serialized in `ovs_vport_cmd_fill_info()`, the fixed-size skb allocated with `NLMSG_DEFAULT_SIZE` overflows, causing `nla_put()` to fail with `-EMSGSIZE` and triggering `BUG_ON(err < 0)` in `datapath.c`.

Code statements information:
.The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
if (!nla_len(ids) || nla_len(ids) % sizeof(u32))
    return -EINVAL;
```
Reason: The above check only validates that the PID array is non‑empty and properly aligned, but imposes no upper bound on the number of PIDs. An unprivileged user (via unshare -Urn) can set an arbitrarily large array. Later, when `ovs_vport_cmd_fill_info()` serializes this array into a fixed‑size skb allocated with `NLMSG_DEFAULT_SIZE`, the buffer overflows. The `nla_put()` call fails with `-EMSGSIZE`, and the subsequent `BUG_ON(err < 0)` triggers a kernel panic.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
+	if (nla_len(ids) / sizeof(u32) > nr_cpu_ids)
+		return -EINVAL;
```
Reason: This cap (added right after the alignment check) rejects any PID array larger than `nr_cpu_ids`. It matches the per‑CPU dispatch limit already used by the datapath side, ensuring consistency and preventing the skb overflow. With this bound, the worst‑case reply size can be pre‑computed, and the `BUG_ON` is no longer reachable.
